bets.reason: The only real edge found tonight: two independent real models both lean Under 43.5, averaging to 57.5% vs the -110 market-implied 52.4% -- a genuine +5.1% edge, not a manufactured one. Real injury notes (KC: DE R. Mason Thomas hamstring, OT Josh Simmons back-questionable; DEN: CB Riley Moss ribs-questionable, WR Marvin Mims foot-questionable) support a lower-scoring script rather than change it. No side taken on the moneyline: real market pricing (Chiefs -132/-134, Broncos +112/+113 across two sources) is close to a real model's own estimate (numberFire: Chiefs 52.3%, Broncos 47.7%) -- efficiently priced, no edge to size a pick around.

last_week_graded.selection: 10-leg NFL SGPx parlay (PIT ML; CIN ML; BAL ML; CHI ML; BUF ML; TEN ML; two 2-pick SGPs), +9164 boosted to +13748, $1.00
last_week_graded.lesson: Double-digit-leg parlays are lottery tickets, not a cheat-sheet card -- stacking 10 legs (even mostly favorites) multiplies the real combined probability down to almost nothing, no matter how good the boosted payout number looks.

last_week_graded.selection: 6-leg NFL same-game player-prop parlay, in-game (Mayfield 275+ pass; Over 50.5; Chase Brown 90+ rush+rec; Egbuka 80+ rec; Chase 100+ rec; Burrow 275+ pass), +3300 boosted to +4290, $0.50
last_week_graded.lesson: This was placed live, during the TB-CIN game -- exactly what pre-kickoff-only rule exists to prevent. Only 1 of 6 legs hit (the total); six aggressive player-yardage props stacked together is a low-probability combination even with two productive passing offenses on the field.

last_week_graded.selection: 2-leg live moneyline parlay (BUF Bills live ML +109; TEN Titans live ML +121), +361, $0.50 (crowns/bonus)
last_week_graded.lesson: One leg actually hit (Bills beat Houston 36-31) but the Titans leg didn't (lost 10-23 to the Jets), and a parlay needs every leg to hit -- a reminder that a single-leg miss sinks the whole ticket even when the rest of the card looks right, on top of this being a live in-game bet in the first place.
